top_categories.workout_context: Road-specific control matters at Gran Fondo Hainan. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 130 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Hainan's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before December.
55ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At mile 60 of 130, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
7,221ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
At Gran Fondo Hainan, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Hainan. Train it until it feels boring.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Gran Fondo Hainan. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 130 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 7,221ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
7,221ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

race_overlay.weather: December in Lingao, Danzhou/Yangpu & Wuzhishan, Hainan Island, China — Tropical island with year-round warmth; breezy mornings, sunny middays, possible afternoon showers and rainbows. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, including rain protection and wet-road braking before Gran Fondo Hainan. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Gran Fondo Hainan’s 130 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Gran Fondo Hainan. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Gran Fondo Hainan rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, Race Simulation, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 130 miles of mixed terrain in Lingao, Danzhou/Yangpu & Wuzhishan, Hainan Island, China.
